source: Rocks are made of minerals. Igneous rock forms when melted rock cools, sedimentary rock from layers of sand and mud pressed together, and metamorphic rock when heat and pressure change a rock.
Thinking rocks never change. Over a very long time, rocks melt, wear down, get pressed into new rocks and change again: the rock cycle.
Pick up a pebble. It may have been a mountain, the floor of a sea or melted rock deep underground.
Minerals are natural solids with their own pattern of particles, like quartz, mica or salt. Rocks are made of one or more minerals. There are three kinds of rock, named for how they form.
The rock cycle: any kind of rock can become any other, over a very long time.
Fossils are found mostly in sedimentary rock, because plants and animals were buried in the soft layers before they hardened.
A rock has layers like a stack of pancakes and a fossil shell in it. Which kind is it most likely?
Layers and fossils come from sediments settling and being pressed.
Thinking rocks never change. Rocks change all the time, only slowly: the rock cycle can take millions of years.
Going further. Agnes Giberne's The World's Foundations is a classic geology book for young readers. Later: The Rock Cycle in Earth Science.
